user_goal: Review whether Operational Clarity can carry a full internal leadership decision deck with enough modern polish and strong proof structure.
primary_risk: The style may feel either too safe and old, or too visual and under-structured for a formal leadership review.

scenario.name: AI Workflow Leadership Decision Deck
scenario.communication_job: Get approval to narrow launch scope to one AI workflow for the next quarter.
scenario.thesis: We should narrow the launch to one workflow because it increases proof density, reduces execution risk, and gives GTM a clearer story.

screens.title: Narrowing the launch to one workflow is the fastest path to proof and lower execution risk.
screens.layout: title block, executive summary table, decision callout
screens.speaker_note_posture: State the decision in the first 20 seconds, then explain why breadth is riskier than it looks.

screens.title: The current broad launch plan asks product, GTM, and enablement to absorb too much ambiguity at once.
screens.layout: left narrative frame, right operating-friction stack
screens.speaker_note_posture: Frame this as coordination cost, not just product scope preference.

frictions: Story too broad to land cleanly
Readiness split across too many paths

screens.title: A focused launch beats a broad release on activation, readiness, and sales clarity.
screens.layout: clustered chart, option table, takeaway strip
screens.speaker_note_posture: Walk left to right through the chart, then land on the operating implication instead of re-reading numbers.

screens.title: The real choice is speed of proof versus breadth of promise.
screens.layout: two-column comparison with four decision rows
screens.speaker_note_posture: Use this to force the tradeoff into the room. Do not let the discussion stay at the level of vague ambition.

screens.title: Approve workflow one now, then unlock expansion only after the first proof cycle is complete.
screens.layout: recommendation box, risk/mitigation panel, milestone row
screens.speaker_note_posture: End on the decision, the risk, and the exact trigger for expansion so the deck feels actionable.

sample_data.risk: Stakeholders may interpret narrower scope as lower ambition.
sample_data.mitigation: Pre-commit the expansion trigger and show the second workflow path in appendix.

screens.title: Appendix: proof assumptions, launch trigger, and workflow-two expansion path.
screens.layout: three appendix panels with smaller evidence blocks
screens.speaker_note_posture: Only pull this up when challenged on assumptions or on what happens after workflow one succeeds.

sample_data.trigger: Expand only after two consecutive proof checkpoints are met.
sample_data.workflow_two: Prepared but not activated in the main story.

open_questions: Does this style need a bit more premium visual contrast for high-stakes internal decks?
Should the comparison slide be more table-like or more narrative?
Is the appendix posture disciplined enough to keep the main deck clean?
